.azure_sql: Talks to Azure SQL Database through the mssql driver's TDS protocol, not an HTTP API
.buildkite: MCP connector: all actions go through Buildkite's hosted MCP server (https://mcp.buildkite.com/direct) via the MCP client, not ctx.client. The MCP adapter can record it, but the server's `tools/list` needs authentication, so it stays exempt until credentials exist.
.dynatrace: Dynatrace publishes the Environment API v2 spec only per tenant, behind authentication (https://{env}.live.dynatrace.com/rest/v2/spec.json returns 401 without a token). There is no public copy on docs.dynatrace.com, in the Dynatrace GitHub org or on APIs.guru; the only downloadable files are community dumps of tenant specs, which are not vendor-published.
.graphql: Generic connector: the endpoint and schema are whatever the user configures, so there is no vendor spec to pin
.mongodb: Talks to MongoDB through its driver's wire protocol, not an HTTP API
.mysql: Talks to MySQL through its driver's wire protocol, not an HTTP API
.new_relic: GraphQL-only: every action POSTs a query to NerdGraph (https://api.newrelic.com/graphql, plus the EU and JP regional hosts). The GraphQL adapter can record it, but New Relic serves its schema by introspection behind an API key, so it stays exempt until credentials exist.
.zabbix: JSON-RPC 2.0 API: every call is a POST to a single endpoint ({baseUrl}/api_jsonrpc.php) and the method name is in the request body. Zabbix publishes no OpenAPI/Swagger description, and OpenAPI path templates cannot distinguish its operations.
